transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, it’s not anything too dramatic, I don’t think, but I’ve noticed I’m having trouble catching what people are saying sometimes. Like at the museum, someone will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them, trying to listen, but then I realize I’ve missed the middle part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to run it by me again. It’s a little embarrassing, honestly.
Is this trouble hearing happening in one ear, or both ears equally?
I’m not really sure, to be honest. I haven’t noticed it being one ear more than the other. It just feels like I miss parts of what people say sometimes, if that makes sense.
Do you notice this trouble understanding speech happens more when there's background noise, like at a busy museum or restaurant, compared to quiet settings?

I think it’s probably more noticeable in a busier place, like the museum, yeah. Someone will be talking right to me about the next art walk and I’m trying to pay attention, but then I realize I missed the middle of what they said. It’s not constant or anything, but I do end up asking them to run it by me again sometimes.
Have you noticed any ringing, buzzing, or other noises in your ears along with the trouble hearing?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed ringing or buzzing, at least not anything that stands out. It’s more just… missing what someone said, if that makes sense.
Has this trouble understanding speech come on gradually over the past several months or years, or did it start more suddenly?

It was more gradual, I think. I mean, I really started noticing it being a bother maybe… a little over two years ago—about two years and a few months. It was after my friend died and I ended up handling the museum liaison things by myself. That’s when it started causing more trouble, I guess.
Have you ever had any ear infections, ear surgeries, or injuries to your ears, or do you notice a feeling of fullness or pressure in your ears?

I don’t think so, no. I can’t recall any ear surgeries or injuries or anything like that. Ear infections… maybe as a kid, but nothing I really remember clearly. And I haven’t noticed a fullness or pressure feeling. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
If you cover one ear at a time, do you notice the hearing difficulty is about the same in both ears, or is one ear clearly worse than the other?

I’m not really sure, to be honest. I haven’t tested it carefully like that. It doesn’t feel like one side is obviously worse, at least not that I’ve noticed… but I could try paying attention if that would help.
Does anyone in your family—parents, siblings—have a history of hearing loss, especially one that started at a similar age to yours?

Not that I know of, no. My parents didn’t, at least not anything that started around this age that I remember. I mean, later in life maybe people don’t hear as well, but I don’t know of a family pattern or anything. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Could you tell me how old you are?
Do you notice more trouble hearing higher-pitched sounds, like women's or children's voices or things like a doorbell, compared to lower-pitched sounds?

I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear difference like that. I mean, sometimes voices can be a little harder if there’s other noise, but I can’t honestly say it’s specifically higher-pitched sounds like women’s voices or a doorbell. I’d have to pay closer attention to be sure, if that’s okay.
Have you ever had significant exposure to loud noises over the years—like loud machinery, music, or firearms—either through work or hobbies?

I don’t think so, not anything major. I mean, I’ve been around normal loud things here and there like anybody, but I didn’t work around machinery or use firearms or anything like that regularly. At least nothing that stands out to me as significant. Does that answer what you mean?
Since it started about two years ago, has your hearing continued to gradually get a little worse over time, or has it stayed roughly the same since then?

I’m not completely sure, honestly. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it clearly getting worse month by month or anything. It feels like it’s been more or less the same, maybe with some days where I notice it more than others. But I could be missing it, if that makes sense.

Do you have any ongoing medical conditions, like diabetes or an autoimmune disorder, or are you taking any medications—such as certain antibiotics, chemotherapy drugs, or high-dose aspirin—that can sometimes affect hearing?

Not that I know of, no. I don’t have diabetes or anything autoimmune that I’m aware of, and I’m not on chemotherapy or those kinds of medicines. I don’t think I take anything like high-dose aspirin either. I can double-check my list if that would help, but nothing like that comes to mind.
When someone speaks clearly and at a normal volume, do you still find it hard to make out the individual words, or is it mainly that you need things to be louder to hear them at all?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that out. If someone’s speaking clearly and facing me, I usually do okay, I think. It’s more that I might ask them to say it a little louder or repeat it. I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but I don’t usually feel like the words are completely garbled or anything. Does that make sense?
